Stay-at-home parents, what is a day in your life like?

I thought you would never ask! , Voat! (It's a stay at home parent joke)

Thank you so much for the post. The one thing that can be difficult is being in a child's world as an adult. They are sometimes hard to understand or your friends have a hard time understanding what it is like being a stay-at-home parent. It can be hard to relate to others at times and you can feel like the walls are closing in around you.

I'm the father of 3 young boys. It's challenging in a good way. The days are long and eventful. There is an endless amount of things to work on in the house and with the kids. I do my best to make as many teachable moment’s as possible. Some things are the same every day and some things are very different.

I get up when the kids get up. Usually 7-8 a.m. if I'm lucky. Change drapers, start making breakfast. When the kids are eating I take a 2 min shower. Get dressed and get the kids clothes ready. Get the kids dressed and ready for the day.

Since it is summer time we have been spending a lot of time outside. We have a sandbox so we usually play around in there for the morning. I have a garden close by so I have been bringing the kids out there to talk to them about the garden. I want to teach them some skills that will be useful to them in their life. By 11ish the younger 2 are getting hungry and tired so we go in and make lunch together. After we eat the 2 oldest help clear the table. Take my 2 year old to the potty and kiss him and the little one before nap time.

Nap time is a parent's "special quiet time." It is quite magical when they sleep for 2 hours and I can get a few things done around the house and maybe pretend like I'm 20 again and waste some time on the computer. ;D

When the kids wake up we have a snack and usually head outside again. The afternoons are hot so we usually turn the sprinkler on and run around in it until we are tired or someone gets hurt. Come inside around 5 and start getting dinner ready. The kids play together in their room while I make dinner. We usually have dinner together if Mom doesn't work late. If the kids eat a good dinner and help clean up the dishes and their toys they get to watch a movie. I'm so happy that someone on the internet introduced me to Studio Ghibli! We have almost watched all their movies. Favorites are Ponyo and My Neighbour Totoro!

Put the youngest to bed first. Brush teeth, go potty and read a story If there is time. "Special Mom and Dad time" after the kids go to bed. Do more cleaning, laundry, and get ready for the next day. Then chillax for the last hour and listen to music and think about how I am screwing up as a parent. It's kinda like meditating.

Overall, I can't complain. I have 3 amazing boys and they have taught me so much about life and myself. I never knew I was capable of giving and caring this much. Now I do my best to care for 3.

Sure thing! I wanted to add something for anyone thinking about having children.

Take some time to enjoy the freedom of not having children and cherish it. Take time to think about what kind of life you want your children to have before you have them. Once you have children your life will be permanently changed, if you are doing it right.

One small regret that I have is that I wished we would have waited a little longer until we had our third. We love our family to death but having 3 young kids can be a bit hectic. I think this would have been lessened if we would have waited another year or so.

That being said, have children if you are able. Teaching brings you much fulfilment and it's pretty much the only way to pass what you have learned on to the next generation. If you can't have children I suggest adopting or being a Big Brother or Sister. There are a lot of people out there that need love. If you are capable, give. Putting someone else’s needs above your own gives you an amazing feeling. Thinking of others first is one of the main things that makes some of us much more HUMAN than others.
